report.name: COREP C72.00 — Liquidity Coverage Ratio
report.description: Monthly Liquidity Coverage Ratio: the stock of high-quality liquid assets over stressed 30-day net cash outflows. HQLA is built in SQL; the stressed outflow leg is computed in a SAS engine with a runtime stress scenario.

table.caption: C72.00 — Liquidity Coverage Ratio by stress scenario (reporting month 2026-09)

cdes.definition: Stock of unencumbered high-quality liquid assets divided by total net cash outflows over a 30-day stress horizon, expressed as a percentage.

candidates.why: Final COREP output; percentage form of the mart ratio and matches the C72.00 cell.
Mart ratio one hop upstream, before rescaling to percent.

cdes.expected_story: LCR = total HQLA ÷ stressed net outflows. HQLA is a fully-traceable SQL haircut calculation; the outflow leg is computed in SAS, so that branch of the field trace stops at the SAS boundary until the AI layer reads it.

cdes.aggregation_level: Entity level (SUM of post-haircut security values)
cdes.definition: Total value of unencumbered liquid assets after supervisory haircuts, eligible for the liquidity buffer.

candidates.why: Sum of post-haircut HQLA values; fully traceable through SQL to raw security market values.

cdes.expected_story: total_hqla_eur = SUM(market_value × (1 − haircut)). A fully-traceable SQL calculation from raw securities.

cdes.aggregation_level: Entity level (SUM of stressed deposit outflows)
cdes.definition: Total expected cash outflows less capped inflows over a 30-day combined stress scenario.

candidates.why: Aggregates the SAS outflow engine; the per-deposit formula is opaque until the AI layer reads the DATA step.

cdes.expected_story: outflow_eur = balance × runoff_rate × stress_factor, computed in a SAS DATA step with a runtime scenario. The field trace stops at the SAS boundary until the AI layer recovers the formula.
